root_cause.text: The `persistent_ram_save_old()` function in the pstore/ram subsystem fails to reallocate or resize the `prz->old_log` buffer when the buffer size increases across multiple calls, leading to an out-of-bounds write during `memcpy_fromio()` because the buffer size is unconditionally updated to the new, larger size.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that `persistent_ram_save_old()` previously only allocated `prz->old_log` if it was NULL (`if (!prz->old_log)`). The fix introduces a check (`if (prz->old_log && prz->old_log_size != size)`) to free the existing buffer via `persistent_ram_free_old(prz)` so that a new buffer of the correct size can be allocated before the copy operation.

commit 201e4aca5aa179e6c69a4dcd36a3562e56b8d670
Author: Anton Vorontsov <anton.vorontsov@linaro.org>
Date:   Sat May 26 06:07:49 2012 -0700

    pstore/ram: Should update old dmesg buffer before reading
    
    Without the update, we'll only see the new dmesg buffer after the
    reboot, but previously we could see it right away. Making an oops
    visible in pstore filesystem before reboot is a somewhat dubious
    feature, but removing it wasn't an intentional change, so let's
    restore it.
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the vulnerability by making persistent_ram_save_old() callable multiple times without handling the case where the buffer size increases. Specifically, it only allocates prz->old_log if it is NULL (lines 261-264), but unconditionally updates prz->old_log_size to the new size (line 270) and performs memcpy operations using the new size (lines 271-272). If the buffer size increases on subsequent calls, this leads to an out-of-bounds write on the previously allocated, smaller prz->old_log buffer.
